hypothesis: Large language models (LLMs) can serve as powerful engines for drug-target interaction prediction by leveraging their broad biomedical knowledge to identify disease-relevant protein targets, evaluate candidate molecules, and assess synthetic viability within multi-agent drug discovery pipelines. LLM-based agents have demonstrated the ability to accurately map diseases to clinically validated protein targets (e.g., JAK isoforms and IL-4Rα for atopic dermatitis) and to guide lead identification through integrated virtual screening and retrosynthesis analysis. This suggests that LLM-driven frameworks represent a promising paradigm for automating and accelerating the early stages of drug discovery, from target identification to candidate molecule evaluation.
